topic: Template Metaprogramming and Expression Evaluation at Compile Time
explanation: Template metaprogramming allows computations to be performed at compile time, leveraging the compiler to generate specialized code based on template parameters. This contrasts with runtime computations, offering significant performance gains in certain scenarios.  Understanding how the compiler handles template instantiation, including recursion and specialization, is crucial for effective use and optimization.  The compiler's behavior involves generating code for each specific template instantiation, potentially leading to code bloat if not managed carefully. Memory layout is affected as the compiler incorporates the results of compile-time computations directly into the generated code, eliminating runtime overhead associated with the same calculations. Assembly-level behavior shows the absence of instructions corresponding to the compile-time evaluated expressions. Runtime behavior simply utilizes the pre-computed results embedded by the compiler.
